hero.name: Ankush Sinha
hero.description: I build and optimize data pipelines with AWS, Airflow, PySpark, and SQL. I’ve worked on large-scale migrations, incremental processing, and data quality for PostgreSQL data marts holding over 1 billion historical records.

about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I’m a Data Engineer at Chola MS General Insurance, working with AWS, Apache Airflow, PySpark, and SQL to build and improve production data workflows. My work spans large-scale data migration, configurable incremental loads, data quality, and query performance.

I enjoy turning complex data movement into reliable, measurable systems—from migrating more than a billion historical records to scaling PySpark workloads. I’m interested in opportunities to keep building dependable data platforms and pipelines.

experience.title: Experience
experience.company: Chola MS General Insurance Pvt Ltd · Chennai

projects.name: Customer360 (CX360)
highlights: Unified data from 7–8 sources in PostgreSQL on AWS RDS, migrating more than 1 billion records across 18 years; each table completed loading in under 30 minutes.
Built an automated, parallel Airflow and S3 pipeline from Amazon Redshift to PostgreSQL, reducing costs by 40% versus the previous approach.

Implemented validated, safe table swaps and JSON-configured PySpark Glue incremental loads with watermarking, audit-column filters, and key-based delete-and-insert: zero duplicate records across 20 tables and 40% less production recovery effort.
Reworked SQL joins, CTEs, and filter placement to reduce end-to-end runtime from 2.5 hours to 50 minutes.
Optimized the DLID framework from Python to PySpark, scaling throughput from 8 million rows per hour to 100 million rows in 40 minutes.

projects.name: Customer Satisfaction (CSAT)
highlights: Designed target tables from business requirements, validated primary-key uniqueness, and worked with business users to raise non-null data coverage from 60% to 90%.

projects.name: Inbound Analysis
highlights: Automated S3 CSV ingestion with Airflow, applied business-rule transformations, and integrated existing database data into the same workflow—eliminating manual cleaning and reducing development effort by 40%.

projects.name: Financial Information Provider (FIP)
highlights: Built source-to-staging and staging-to-target ETL pipelines with watermark-based incremental processing, reducing debugging effort by 20%.
Created materialized views that cut API data retrieval from 200 ms to 10 ms and enabled parallel reads and writes to reduce processing time by 40%.
Developed a Python and AWS Glue DLID framework that generates a unique customer identifier used across digital applications; targeted historical reads cut incremental runtime by 70%.
